content:
**__Settling down__**
By the edge of a forest, there's a lake. So far, not touched by people, only by land animals and fish flowing along with the streams supplying the lake with water, and out of it through the river starting its life there. Not a bad place for those who want to live in peace alongside nature, and close to water. That's why there is a curious wooden machine, parked close to the lakeside, with a shifter, a grung holding a baby, and an imp floating by them standing next to it and watching the scenery.

"I like it." Roy says. "What about you?"
Sabrine is distracted for a second, gazing at the scenery. 'Hm? Ah---I agree. It's a beautiful place, and it looks like it has everything we need.'
`Not that that's that much.` Kukudh adds, sticking their tongue out.
"That makes it even better. Should we name this place, or maybe that'd come later?" Roy wonders.
'Well, 'home' sounds like a good name.' Sabrine laughs. 'An actual name that'd go on a map, though... we've got plenty of time to think about that.'
"Something welcoming, that's for sure. Something that reflects what we want this place to be. A home for us, for anyone who wishes to join us, a place where nature is respected. And maybe something about a swarm but that's secondary. Or tertiary."

Sabrine nods, as Kukudh snarks, `Guess you could give people... a swarm welcome.`
Roy pauses in silence while looking directly at Kukudh. "You are strictly not incorrect. Perhaps at some point we should go downstream and see if anyone lives further down. I'm curious if maybe the river already has a local name. Maybe it'll give us an idea for our place."
'That's a good idea...' Sabrine hands baby Amaranth to Roy, and slips into the lake. 'This water feels good, clean. I don't think we'll need to find more parts like for the Hudson.'
"We'll just need to take good care of it from start. And I'll need to get us some lumber for a small house. Good thing we already have some experience from helping Fuddles and Secel. And good thing that until we're done we have the Strider."
'I mean - worst-case scenario, we've got enough blankets to make Ammy a comfortable bed, if nothing else.' Sabrine gazes at the sleeping child in Roy's arms. 'I might have slept on dirt, not even grass, but she deserves better.'
"Yeah. And gotta make some guest houses too. Can't have a housewarming party if we don't invite Ed and Irynx."
'Absolutely.' Sabrine leans back, sinking into the water, as Kukudh takes a stick and starts sketching vague plans in the dirt. `Gotta have a good kitchen... room for expansion... hey, we could make a gazebo...`
"Perhaps. Hmm, not sure why but I just thought of old table from the Ordinary. Anyway, let's eat something before we start planning how to set things up."


------------

**__Village school__**
'So, who can tell me the benefits of bugs to the ecosystem?' Sabrine gestures with a hand made of water to the half-dozen children (and Kukudh) sat in front of her and Roy - two of their three, Peri and Carnelian, and the others living nearby.
A few of the kids raise their hand, and one of them upon being selected says, shyly, "Um... Do they help flowers?"
'They do!' Sabrine nods approvingly. 'They, ah... what was the word... Well, they help the flowers grow more flowers.'

"Pollinate." Roy interjects. "That's the word you were looking for. But, it's not all bugs that do that. Bees, for example, do, same with wasps. But then you have things like ants. Who can tell me where ants make their colonies?"
'Uh, um, they live in mountains, right?' 'Nah, mountains are too big. They live in tiny little burrows!' The kids start debating.
Sabrine waits for them to finish, before answering, 'While yes, mountains themselves are too big - you were on the right track, both of you. If you've seen any small mounds of dirt around, that might be an anthill they made to live in! Just be careful when playing near them, ants will bite to defend their homes, so it's best not to disturb them.'
"Yep, ants are crafty, and great at teamwork." Roy continues. "But, underground is not the only place you can find them. Some kinds make their homes in tree crowns, putting together their small castles out of leaves they glue together."
Even Sabrine looks fascinated, like she didn't know this; the kids are in awe. 'Wow!'

"The important thing is, they know the tree is their home, and they care for it, protecting it from parasites and other creatures that would damage the tree. Everyone benefits from that cooperation. Nature's full of examples of teamwork like that, and we should remember to both look into nature for inspiration, and cooperate with nature ourselves."

One of the kids from the neighboring farms raises their hand. "Mister Roy, how do you know so much about bugs?"
Kukudh laughs. `This's gonna be good~`
"Well..." Roy's coat starts slightly moving, and his kids look at one another knowingly before the swarm spreads from the pockets to form into streams circling around its keeper. "There are more benefits to cooperating with nature than you think, even if you expect them." Peri and Carn high-five each other with their swarm hands to the other kids' surprise.

'Oh, that's how Ammy gets stuff off the top shelf!' One of the kids has a startling revelation, Sabrine nods, laughing. 'Caused us more trouble than we expected when she was small. She picked it up so naturally - a lot easier than I did, even. Peri and Carn here are learning just as fast.' She gestures to the high-fiving shifters.
"Don't worry about it, though. Everyone can find their place in nature. Now, I think it's time for a break. How about a goodberry break by the lake?"
'Yeah!' The kids (and Kukudh) chant in unison, rushing for the shore.



------------

**__Home worth defending__**
The three children shelter in the house, trying to ignore the noise from outside, Kukudh perching on Amaranth's shoulder. `Alright. You remember where the emergency teleport glyph is, yes?`
'I-in the back room, right?' Carnelian, the youngest, pipes up. Kukudh nods. `Yeah. And you know where it'll take you if you need to use it?`
'Isn't it Murry Hill?' Peri asks. `Right again. Okay. The most important question. Ammy, you can use it if needed?`
Amaranth nods, shivering, but prepared to protect her siblings.
`Right. Ammy, Peri, Carn - if I tell you, or if I disappear - run for the teleport glyph. When you're at the park, go and find Aunty Fuddles, let her know something's happened at the village.`

Meanwhile, outside the village, Roy's running around a large monstrosity and pelting it with arrows from all sides while Sabrine aims her staff, sending a cone of freezing cold through as many tentacles and eyeballs as she can. The two had set up a combination of Plant Growth and Spike Growth around the creature, to keep it from getting any closer to the village.

"Resilient bugger, isn't it?" Roy shouts to Sab. She nods grimly, chanting, as the plants and spikes are joined by wrathful kelp, entangling as many tentacles as it can; hidden in the assorted plants, a watery imp lurks with a scythe. 'Kukudh's keeping the kids safe, now it's up to us to keep the village safe.'
"Great. Look out, behind you!"
'Ah!' Sabrine jumps to the side, barely avoiding a tentacle to the neck, though taking a painful blow through her armour in the process. The kelp flickers, but remains intact. 'It won't... quit, huh? Gil, give us strength...'

A bright glow, and she transforms, seeming to become made of water and kelp as Gil once was, large aqueous wings forming from her back.
"No you don't!" Roy's swarm explodes from his coat, and with a hand motion he directs it right at the aberration to engulf it in an Insect Plague. He shifts and runs over to Sabrine. "Sab, you okay?"
'I'm holding on. This should work for a while, water's... surprisingly resilient.' She swoops upwards to fire blasts of frigid water at any eyeball she can see.

"Freezing it seems to be working. Let's double down on that." Noticing the monster's up to something, Roy surrounds Sab with his coat and rolls away from where tentacles were about to slam. "Going in." Roy runs closer towards the thing and nearly point-blank blasts it with another cone of frigid air that flows right through it, engulfing a big part of its body in ice. "Shatter!"
Sabrine nods, and focuses all the power she can into her blunderbuss. 'You stay away from our people!' Her voice rises to a scream as the blunderbuss fires a burst of piercing sound, the resulting vibrations visible in her watery form.

The extremities of the thing's body fall to the ground as the frozen core, holding its vital organs, shatters to many tiny pieces. Roy takes a few steps back to look at any signs of motion, but there don't seem to be any anymore. "Everyone alright back there?"
'I-i-i-i-m-m-m al-l-lr-r-r-i-i-i-g-gh-t.' The aftershocks are still rippling through Sabrine, an odd thing to witness.

Roy waves to some magpies. "Hey. Have you seen any more of these while flying around? ... Okay, great, thanks. Come over for some seeds in a bit." He goes back to Sab. "Let Kukudh know the kids can come out, it's fine now."

As the vibrations cease, she coalesces back to her normal self; 'Got it. Though, ah--- looks like they know.'
The children come out of the house, cheering, Kukudh perching on Amaranth's shoulder. `They insisted on watching. I'm not sure it was the best idea, but hey, they worried less and means they'd understand why if they had to run.`
"Well, I hope you enjoyed the show. Now, who wants to help me move all the pieces into one place so we can burn them?"
'I, ah, should go and remove my armour. I need to check on that injury.'
"Need some healing? If not, I'll start cleaning up."

Sabrine shrugs. 'I'll see, but - it doesn't feel like it's urgent, at least. Without the armour, would've been a lot worse.' she heads into the house. Kukudh also has mysteriously disappeared.
Roy nods, wild shapes into a bear, and starts dragging pieces into the fireplace outside the village.

He ponders how good it'd be for fertilizing the soil for the plants. Probably too eldritch.



------------

**__The more the merrier__**
Even after decades of growth, the village has never had this many people show up at one time. You, an old friend from the City, happened to come by for a visit at the same time as... a warren full of jackalopes, by the looks of it, as well as quite a few others. Luckily, Kukudh offers to guide you around - huh, that imp's gotten a lot politer since the last time you saw them.

`Okay, so - you've met Ammy before, right?`
Amaranth, you definitely remember. She takes after her mother, looking somewhat froggish with piercing blue eyes. Behind her are two strange Grung, both with tails (you suppose that runs in the family) - one of them, introduced as Safira, is an ordinary Grung height, with wild 'hair' and a swarm of bugs giving her a jittery appearance. She offers you a high-five, which you accept. The other - who has his face buried in a book - is extremely tall, taller even than his mother. He summons a magical hand to wave to you without looking up, as Amaranth introduces him as Octavian.
Nearby is Corbianne, Irynx's daughter - you haven't seen her in a while, either. You hope she's alright. Safira and Octavian refer to her as Aunty; you suppose that growing up together for a bit made her and Amaranth consider each other sisters.

`Oh hey, Peri! You met our friend yet?'
You have indeed met Periwinkle--- 'Peri. Just Peri.' Did he know what you were thinking...? Fine, you have met Peri before, but only when he was very small. He's grown up considerably, though still somewhat strange - you know all of Roy and Sabrine's children are shifters, like the kids in Ferrytown, but you've heard Peri becomes some... strange animal, the likes of which you've only heard in rumours, some sort of a hybrid of a duck, a beaver, and an otter...?
His child, Apricot, is a cheerful young girl with prominent front teeth, whittling on a piece of wood. 'It's called a platypus, by the way.' Wait, is she telepathic too? 'No, I just have good intuition.' You can't tell if she's being serious...

`And this is the youngest, Carn - Carnelian - and their son Jasper!`
Carnelian bows politely; they're holding a half-orc baby, and you can really see the resemblance. The same thick skin, the same wide faces, what animal did those traits come from again? Some... hippocrates thing that lives in the swamps? You're not completely sure.
An orc lady comes over to bring them food; Carnelian introduces her as their wife, Alizarin, before she leaves again to get herself a plate. Carn themselves gives off a pretty chill vibe, you spend a while talking to them.

At some point, you notice the literal sea of jackalopes surrounding Roy and Sabrine has dispersed, and you can finally go and talk to them like you originally intended.
They look older, definitely - it's especially noticeable on Sabrine since her hair and skin used to be so bright and vibrant, and you suppose Grung especially don't live quite as long as a lot of races; shifters longer, but still below average. A reason why you wanted to visit before it was too late.
You talk with them for a long time, updating them on your life and learning about theirs in the years since you've seen them, before---
`Wow, it got late. We got a guesthouse you can stay in, even with all of Ed and Will's kids hanging out here.` Kukudh interrupts. Will? That must be the tabaxi you've seen hanging around.
Well - everyone clearly looks tired. You can always continue your conversations tomorrow. You're prepared to stay a few days if allowed, even... honestly, you feel you could almost live in this village, even with how different it is to the City. Perhaps tomorrow, you can think about it some more...



------------

**__Duty continues__**
It's been about two or three years since the last time Roy and Sab had been to Empire City. Fortunately, the teleportation circle set up with Irynx's help made it so the trip would be quick and painless. A lot of things have changed, but many still stayed the same, especially Murry Hill Park, to where the mender and the priestess were called for a meeting with the representatives of the Masons.

It appeared there was another job to do, at the south coast, to assist the Tinkers with repairing the damage caused by a hurricane. It would be a week-long excursion, or at least that was the expectation.

Ended up, surprisingly, to be just within the expected time. Over the years with different tasks, everyone was able to gain experience with mending cornerstones, and with teamwork between the three groups, everything could go swimmingly, giving Roy and Sab some time to enjoy the sights from the airship trip back.

From up there, along the east coast, you could see the growth of the States, but also the clear boundaries where the wilderness started. At least for now, things looked great, and the two hoped they'd stay that way as long as possible.



------------

**__Kukudh's wish__**
'Kukudh, you're sure you want to do this?'

Kukudh is chilling on a floating rocking chair. `Yeah, I'm sure. Someone's gotta look after everyone, right?`
A tired Sabrine sits on the bed, facing them. Her 'hair' is greying, her bright skin fading, almost to the degree of her old Reborn self - though still with one piercing blue eye, and without the aura of desperation that used to stick to her in that form.
"You just want to be an uncontrollable force of snark, don't you." Roy jokingly remarks to the imp.
`Hey, back in my day, you appreciated my snark.` Kukudh sticks their tongue out and waves a gnarled stick-gun in the air.
'And you're sure you understand the procedure, and the possible consequences?'

Kukudh thinks for a minute before responding. `Yeah. So when you, uh, move on, I'll still be bound to Roy and stay behind. Then he's got to bind me to himself and someone else, and people go on like that. But there's the risk I might end up in pain, or permanently separated from you. But hey, if I get separated I can still come find you eventually, right?`
'You'd likely be on minimal capabilities, like any random summoned familiar rather than a Guide. And if you died at that point, you likely wouldn't be able to come back.'
`Yeah, yeah. I get it. But someone's gotta be the leader of the swarm, you know them well~` They start bonking their stick in a rhythm.
"Well, if you're sure. You may have been a bit of a pain sometimes, but you're still part of the family and I don't want you to suffer."
`Uh, I think 'a bit' is an understatement. But yeah, gotta make up for that.` Sabrine stares at them, clearly having a telepathic conversation. `Okay, okay, I already did. But hey, someone's gotta look after you.`
"Your choice, buddy. Let's get you that child's wish granted."
`Aw, you remembered!` They have a genuine smile. `Don't worry. I got this. Let's get this ritual started.`



------------

**__Life before your eyes (Sabrine)__**
Sabrine drifts, calm though blinded by the light, a faint lullaby in the background, an odd sense of familiarity mixed into the unknown. For some reason, her first thought is about it being nice to have eyelids.

Memories float by. The birth of her fifth grandchild, Olive, Jasper's younger sister. Visits from old friends, with news of the City when it became too difficult for her to visit often. The calm of the lakeside garden, occasionally punctuated with the noises of happy children playing. Saving a visitor from the frozen lake, when the ice broke as they ran to catch their dog.
Her last duty as Gil's high priestess, passing the role - and her staff and blunderbuss - to Ruto of Murry Hill, with Peri working alongside his and Darunia's son Saria as an apprentice. Her last dance, just days ago. She was weak, and couldn't stand for long, but Roy supported her, picked her up when her legs failed, with all of the care - no, even more care than they had had for each other so long ago.
'I hope he'll be alright...' A tinge of sadness and worry starts to permeate the blinding void, before---

A sudden touch to her nose, a radiating warmth and feeling of peace. She opens her eyes - the light is still there, but despite it, she can see a small pseudodragon, and memories come flooding back. 'Ah, Lucy. It's been a while. Then the music must be Bo? I apologise, I suppose this is more... disorienting for me than for most. Fourth time in this situation and all the circumstances were different.'
Bo chuckles, offering her a glass of apple juice, though Lucy looks a little confused - on her behalf, Bo inquires as to Kukudh.
'Ah---that might also explain the disorientation. Looks like the ritual worked.' Sabrine takes a sip of fresh, pure juice before continuing, 'They're staying in the world of the living for now, to help out our family. We aren't sure how long the double summoning ritual will work for, but they're aware of the risks... if and when they show up, hopefully they'll find their way back to me somehow. And, well, if you see them, you know where I'll be.'

'Ah---' Sabrine is suddenly aware of a small plush imp on her person, crudely made yet clearly with love. She offers the plush to Lucy, who squeals in joy. 'Looks like I brought gifts.' A ukulele manifests itself in her hands, which she presents dramatically to Bo.
At her side is a battered wooden revolver, the text engraved on it now illegible. 'I suppose it would be strange for anyone else to use this, now. Be free.' A gesture from her, and the revolver dries out, dissolving into dust.

'So, I suppose this is it. The whole 'life flashes before your eyes' thing, that's now? I suppose it'll include before my first death, too?' Bo nods, and she continues, 'Well, I also brought... what did Kukudh call this revolutionary invention? Popped corn? Regardless. Most of this is as much of a surprise to me as it is to you... Just please, don't judge me too harshly for it.'

The carpet moves through illusions of a life - a life unremembered, not even truly belonging to Sabrine, but a life nonetheless. She's mostly silent, though making the occasional comment, such as 'Wow, is that what my name used to be? I'm glad I didn't remember that.'
Only twice does she lose her composure; once, rewatching the memory of her sister's death, and the other, watching herself in an awful state, making a pact with the *Thing* in order to survive the guilt. Both times, Lucy comforts her, but she can't face Bo.

Her true life goes a lot more smoothly, albeit with a couple of awkward moments - Kukudh's spying on Malathor, for one, as well as the Heore situation. But here, she's a lot more animated - seeing her family and friends again, laughing at Kukudh and Orphy's antics, crying with joy rewatching the births of her children, nodding in quiet reflection at the lessons learned along the way.

As the journey ends, Sabrine thanks Bo, and asks just one question. 'Do you think... I've atoned for my past?'
'Well now... that's a question, only yerself kin answer.' Bo responds, smiling. 'Do you?'
Sabrine freezes for a second, not expecting this, before taking a deep, unnecessary breath: 'I do. Thank you.'

'Gil, I'm coming home. Take care of everyone for me.'



------------

**__Life before your eyes (Roy)__**
A swarm of insects flies through somewhere, before coming across a pseudodragon.
"Oh, hi, Lucy. Hi, Bo." The swarm buzzes. "That's where you two had gone after everything that happened in the city. At least some stable job, right?"
The buzzing sounds like laughter, as the ferryman looks with confusion.
"Oh, don't worry. It's not the first time for us like this. That's apparently how my spirit looked to Gil back when he revived me. Looks like he wasn't that far off. Or it's some Warden stuff in play now. Who knows?"
The swarm coalesces into the form of Roy.

"This will be a bit more convenient, I suppose. I've heard stories about the ferryman who watches your life alongside you during the ride to the other side. Well, if it's been you this whole time, I don't need to worry about Sab. Back then I wished I could've gone with her, but putting an eternal guilt on her for doing that to myself is not really something I'd do. So, recap?"
Images of a small town in central Europe show up. Roy as a youngster, already messing around with machines. It doesn't look that bad.
"Yeah. It wasn't bad. I enjoyed my time there. Had a family, had some friends, and my hobby. Just that I wasn't really a favorite of the adults, cause I didn't really care about things they did. But given I was the oldest kid of my parents, I was expected to take over their boring part in running the town. Just not my thing. And I wouldn't have minded."

The scene changes to Roy behind a corner, listening in on his parents and grandparents talking about what they decided on the greater swarm's gathering. There are mentions of getting him out of the picture, and not caring about whether he succeeds on his assigned task in Arcania.
"Yep. I don't think they really knew that I found out. But it's okay. I wanted to go anyway. See new places, meet new people. And if I were to succeed in establishing the swarm's presence across the ocean, that'd just be a bonus, not a main goal."

Next images show Roy devastated to have to give away the longbow he made, having people abandon the conversation when he talks about his swarm on the cruise to Arcania, and later in pubs in the City, him working quietly on engines at the docks, and at one point unconscious drunk on the floor inside the Red Aphid. Roy just shrugs to Bo. "Going from being part of a community to completely on your own isn't easy."

Soon afterwards the events reach the point of Roy's first untimely death.
"Desperation's a killer. I probably never would've tried that if I felt like I belonged anywhere. I just wanted a place to call home again." Roy shrugs again, but with a visibly happier expression. "Through this though, I did find one."

The events of the campaign for Empire City move through in front of them. Events Bo's been part of, events he missed, events he could not have seen in the mender's cottage.
"Well, I promised the mender at the time to not tell anyone. But afterwards it'd been up to me to invite people there, so consider yourself invited now."
Discussions about the cornerstones flow by, attempts to fix things with very little knowledge, as well as...

"Yep. Gil wanted to invite you too. You had our recommendation. That's the impression you had made. We might have had disagreements about Mal, and couldn't all know everything, but I'm glad everything worked out in the end."
Weeks of the revolution fly by, including Sab's death due to Heore's experiment. The two exchange some thoughts about the whole ordeal. "Wait, that was you? Well done, you fooled us all."

Next months fly by, with the work on the City, talking with the Masons as the new Mender, a visit to the forge, the water pumps, the Blue Strider, and finally the departure.

Bo gets to watch all the beautiful sights of the lands west of the new nation, the adventures shared with Ed and Irynx, the settling down with a family and starting his own little swarm village far from any troubles of the wide world, with only occasional trips out to fulfill his duty to Arcania and Gil as the next Mender.

Being more stay-at-home and assigning his successor after Sabrine's passing, so he can watch over their family more. Visits from old friends every now and then so Roy feels less alone nearing the end of his time.

"Yeah, overall I'm happy with how it ended up. You know, there were times where I considered using the knowledge I got as a druid to try to prolong our lives, but... Just as much as Gil stepped back wherever he could to give us all a chance to forge our present, it's time for the next ones to replace us. And for me to finally have a reunion. Thanks for the ride, Bo. Take care of yourself."

Roy leaves Bo a batch of berries, and steps off the carpet towards new unknown, to find a home and Sabrine once again.



------------
------------

Thank you everyone for this journey we've all had.

Also in a few hours (before the deadline of course), when Crui wakes up, we'll post our other bits of prose, those were originally to go at the start of our epilogues, as sort of intro/teaser, but when we decided to collab on <#880280609170264084> these just didn't really fit well.
***Bonus parts:***

This is your first time back to the City in years - and wow, it's really changed. You suppose the war had something to do with that: not being a fighter, you were waiting for it to end before returning home.  But even with this being the place you grew up, and you being used to its... oddities... it's difficult to fully accept all the rumours going around. The British, rebellions, even pigeon uprisings you can believe. T-rexes, archdevils, people coming back from the dead, giant... cannons that shoot electricity... that can't be real, right? That sounds like a war crime.
Still, though, the first thing you should do is check on your family. Not that you know where they might be now... Probably best to look into official records. And where better for that than the library?

Though your ASL is a little rusty, you successfully manage to communicate with the librarians unscathed, and they direct you to the records section. But you notice that a lot of the books about the last decade or so seem to be missing from the shelf - but the librarians would have told you if they were checked out, right? You take one of the books which remain, and go to sit down and browse through it.
As you find a seat, though, you notice something odd. There's a pale purple Grung woman sitting at one of the tables, a pile of books twice her size on the floor next to her, and a - much smaller, probably about two or three total - pile of books with bookmarks in sitting on the table. As you watch, curious, she shakes her head, and puts the book she's reading on the large pile with a... well, it's not the most impressive hop you've ever seen from a Grung, but it's good enough.
You quickly finish the one book you have, and stand up, waiting for her to notice you - you'd rather not just take a book from the pile, out of politeness, but also a bit of fear: first, you remember the time you accidentally made a small sound as a child. The librarians had mercy then, but would they now, either for you if the pile fell, or the stranger if she was startled and croaked? And second... you can't explain why, but something about this small, cute, unassuming frog... scares you. You try to think why, but then---

A faint sound of buzzing, faint enough the librarians don't seem to mind. A humanoid man walks into the area, a strange pigeon perching on his shoulder, and his clothes looking to be slightly... crawling? The woman looks up at the same time, as if she knew he would be there; she waves, and he 'speaks' in slightly clumsy ASL, 'How's the search going?'
The Grung shrugs and stretches, before responding clumsily, spelling out some words; 'It's... done. Lovlatar didn't go anywhere. And Louhi... the only source I can find for it is...' her hands shake a little, as if it's strange to think about. 'My own obituary.'
...wait, did you see that right? Her obituary? She doesn't look dead, or even like one of those 'Reborn' people you heard about. She just looks like an ordinary purple Grung, albeit with - now you look - one piercing blue eye, and one dull grey one. Huh. As you look, though, she makes eye contact with you, and looks a little startled for a second - noticing you flinching in fear, though, she gives you a reassuring smile and signs, 'Apologies. Did you need any of these books?'

You respond to her that you're looking for your family, and her eyes widen in surprise, spelling slowly, 'Thompson? A relative of Thomas Forease Thompson, by any chance?'
At the sight of your brother's name, you're shocked. The last you heard from your brother is that he was loyal to the old King - a sentiment you wholly disagreed with, which is why you left. Even if you had a hope of reconciling, you assumed he was dead, or worse. But now...? The woman nods to the strange pigeon, who flies off.
'My Guide is going to find him. If you'd like to meet up, I know he'd be happy to - just come to Murry Hill Park. It's not my place to tell you any of his story, just know... he has been a great help to us. Blessings of [unintelligible] to you both.'
she takes the man's hand, and they leave the library, as you try to determine what her sign means - it seems to be a combination of the words for 'sand', 'fish', and 'warden'...

You shrug. It's something to ask your brother about, you guess. Now, hopefully that cafe he liked is still standing...

You've been here before several times, by the banks of the Hudson. Quite a nice place, with benches and trees. Great to take a break. Even if you haven't done much today, again. You're young, you still don't know what you want to do. But this time, at this hour, you happened to notice someone walking into one of those small wooden booths. You've never really paid any attention to them, and now there's someone entering one, with a can of essence fuel and some odd fine mesh. You wanted to go home soon, but you're too curious to stop watching now.

After a moment, they leave it, with a visibly emptier can, and a mesh just like that, but dirtier. You watch them go far away, and the desire to know gets you to walk up to the booth after making sure nobody's watching you.

The wood's quite old, but well preserved. There are pipes going between the booth and the river, going almost all the way to the riverbed, as you can see in the clear water. You're wondering what might be inside, when you notice... the door isn't locked. You peer inside.

There's an engine. An airship engine. Only much smaller than you've seen, even on the smallest skiffs. Was it taken apart and reassembled? Looking around, you notice one of those meshes, in a valve of a pump. It hits you. That's a filter, and the engine is powering a pump.

This is a water-filtering station. All these small booths along the length of the river must be that too.
You've heard that during the independence war, the river was horribly contaminated, with damnation from old Hampstead leaving nasty gunk to flow downstream. You found it hard to believe - the river's been clean for as long as you remember.

But this looks operational. And someone's clearly maintaining it. They can't be just duds for show, right? Something about this look odd. You feel like you're being watched, but there's nobody around. But there doesn't seem to be any malice in that potential observer. You decide to leave the booth and close it behind you. You take another look at it from the outside from different sides. There seems to be text on some planks. They're rearranged, and the letters don't fully line up, but you think you can picture how they should be.

"Red Aphid"

Huh. It sounds like a ship name, you think. The curiosity gets the better of you and you run along the river to check other booths.

"The Nightingale"

"The Nimble"

"The Dread Not"

"The Strix"

And several others farther along the banks. These are all airships. Or were. And they've been turned into these water purifying stations, apparently. Have they been running since the war? Whose ships were they? You want to know. It's getting late, so you'll visit the library tomorrow.

That night you sleep really well. You dream of the river, and of some warm feeling coming from it. When you wake up, for the first time in a while, your mind is fully made up.
